title: How an LLM is served on Kubernetes GPUs
subtitle: A request enters the cluster, a cache-aware router picks GPU pods, and prefill and decode run on separate workers.
hook: Splitting prefill from decode cut P99 inter-token latency from 900 ms to 100 ms.

sources.title: KV Cache-Aware Routing and P/D Disaggregation on Kubernetes
sources.speaker: Yuchen Fama & Ashish Kamra

sources.title: What Is an Inference Engine, Anyway?
sources.speaker: Charles Frye

nodes.label: Agent client
nodes.detail: Coding agents send turn after turn that reuse the same system prompt and tool definitions. The team studied traces from SWE-bench and real Claude Code sessions, from a few turns up to 3,000.
nodes.tradeoff: Cache hit rates often exceed 90%, and input can be over 100 times the output.

nodes.label: Cluster gateway
nodes.detail: The request enters the Kubernetes cluster at a gateway, which hands it to the router. llm-d is a Kubernetes-native inference framework under the CNCF, and the model servers run as pods (containers) in the cluster.
nodes.tradeoff: Default Kubernetes scheduling, which ignores the cache, was the slowest baseline in Red Hat's tests.

nodes.label: KV-aware router
nodes.detail: llm-d's endpoint picker keeps probing each vLLM pod: running and waiting requests, KV cache use, and which prompt prefixes are cached. It sends the request to a lightly loaded pod most likely to get a cache hit.
nodes.tradeoff: In the demo a cold turn took about 3 seconds; a turn reusing the cached system prompt took about 1.

nodes.label: Prefill workers
nodes.detail: Pods running the vLLM inference engine on GPUs. Prefill processes the full prompt in one compute-heavy, bursty pass and builds its KV cache; the engine's scheduler batches requests so the GPU stays busy.
nodes.tradeoff: On an agentic workload with a 45:1 input-to-output ratio, 2 prefill + 1 decode workers gave 4x faster first token and 60% more requests.

nodes.label: KV transfer
nodes.detail: The prefill worker outputs KV transfer metadata. The decode worker uses it to pull the computed KV cache across the network fabric.
nodes.tradeoff: Needs a fast fabric such as RDMA or RoCE; without one, the speakers advise staying with aggregated serving.

nodes.label: Decode workers
nodes.detail: Separate vLLM pods generate one token at a time from the transferred cache. Decode is memory-bandwidth hungry and latency sensitive, so keeping long prefills off these GPUs stops them stalling the token stream.
nodes.tradeoff: Splitting prefill from decode cut P99 inter-token latency from about 900 ms to 100 ms on 16 H100s.

nodes.label: KV cache tiers
nodes.detail: The KV cache stores attention state for tokens already processed, so a shared prefix is not recomputed. llm-d is adding offload tiers like NVMe SSD and KV stores like Mooncake, plus session-aware eviction.
nodes.tradeoff: Frye treats heavy spilling to CPU memory and disk like OS swap: a sign the deployment is under-provisioned.

nodes.label: Pod metrics
nodes.detail: Each vLLM pod reports queue depth and KV cache use, which the router reads. Dashboards track time to first token and inter-token latency per replica.
nodes.tradeoff: In Frye's traffic spike, queuing raised time to first token, then inter-token latency, until new replicas came online.

nodes.label: Autoscaler
nodes.detail: Watches capacity and the live traffic mix, then scales prefill and decode pods up or down independently.
nodes.tradeoff: A fixed prefill-to-decode ratio is only a start; it has to shift with traffic.

flow.text: A coding agent sends its next turn with the same long system prompt.
The request enters the Kubernetes cluster through the gateway.
The endpoint picker chooses pods by load and cached prefix.
vLLM reads the prompt on GPU, reusing cached KV, and builds the rest.
The decode pod pulls the KV cache over the fast network.
vLLM streams tokens back; P99 gap between tokens about 100 ms.
Pod metrics update; the autoscaler adds pods if queues grow.

takeaways.text: Cache-aware routing alone beat default Kubernetes scheduling, before splitting prefill and decode.
Separating prefill and decode made P99 inter-token latency about nine times better: 900 ms to 100 ms.
Disaggregation is a trade-off: best at mid concurrency with long prompts, and needs RDMA-class networking.
